#web_credential_install_types: The editions that have a dashboard, and therefore require tpot_web_password.
It is NOT the list of types that put a credential on upstream's command line:
upstream is always invoked as the sensor type and never receives one at all.
The credential is written into T-Pot's own .env afterwards, from standard input.

keys.name: tpot_os_user
keys.help: The unprivileged account that owns the T-Pot checkout and runs upstream's installer.

keys.name: tpot_os_user_password_policy
keys.help: locked leaves the OS account with no usable password; set gives it the one below. set does NOT make sudo prompt: upstream's unattended mode refuses to run without a passwordless grant, so the grant stays either way.

keys.name: tpot_os_user_password
keys.help: SECRET. The OS account password, hashed before it reaches the shadow file. Only used when the policy is set, and it buys an interactive login only.

keys.name: tpot_sudo_nopasswd
keys.help: Whether the OS account may sudo without a password. It must be true and is no longer derived from the password policy: upstream's unattended mode runs `sudo -n -k true` and aborts the install before changing anything when it fails, so false yields no install rather than a prompting one. Stated, never inherited.

keys.name: tpot_web_user
keys.help: The dashboard username. Defaults to the value of tpot_os_user. No colon: the credential is stored as a user:hash record and upstream sanitises the name only on its interactive path, which this installer never takes.

keys.name: tpot_web_password
keys.help: SECRET, and the only required input. The dashboard password. Not accepted as a flag value, and it never reaches any command line: upstream is driven as a sensor install, which never asks for it, and this project hashes it with htpasswd -n -i from standard input.

keys.name: tpot_os_upgrade
keys.help: none skips it, safe runs apt upgrade, full runs apt dist-upgrade.

keys.name: tpot_timezone
keys.help: The timezone to set, or null to leave the box alone.

keys.name: tpot_locale
keys.help: The locale to generate and set, or null to leave the box alone. Applied after T-Pot is installed. Never C or POSIX: ansible-core exits 1 under a non-UTF-8 locale.

keys.name: tpot_max_map_count
keys.help: The vm.max_map_count sysctl the search engine requires.

keys.name: tpot_ansible_source
keys.help: Where ansible-core comes from. auto uses the distribution package when it is new enough, and builds a pinned virtualenv otherwise, which is what makes the older legacy-tier releases work.

keys.name: tpot_ansible_core_spec
keys.help: The pip requirement used when the virtualenv path is taken.

keys.name: tpot_normalize_line_endings
keys.help: Normalise CRLF and remove archive debris from this tree before running.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_ref
keys.pattern_help: a FULL 40-character lowercase commit sha of upstream T-Pot -- not a tag, not a branch, not an abbreviated sha. A tag makes upstream's own re-run check compare the tag NAME against the commit sha git checked out, so every second run exits 1; an abbreviated sha fails the same way. roles/tpot_install refuses anything else before it fetches, so a value this pattern let through would fail an hour later instead of now. Run tools/pin-upstream.sh, which resolves a tag or branch to the sha and writes everything derived from it.
keys.help: A FULL 40-character commit sha of upstream T-Pot. Never a tag and never a branch: upstream resolves a detached checkout to a commit sha and compares it against what you asked for, so a tag mismatches itself on every second run. Shipped unset; tools/pin-upstream.sh produces it. ONE VARIABLE PINS TWO THINGS: the install.sh this project fetches and verifies, and the -b argument that pins the payload upstream clones. They may never be set apart, because with no -b upstream silently resolves its own default branch. It also decides the supported tier, because upstream gates on /etc/os-release before it reads any flag. It does NOT pin the container images: those carry a mutable tag from .env and are re-pulled at every start.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_url
keys.help: Where upstream's install.sh is fetched from. Derived from the ref, which is the safe state; override it only to fetch the SAME ref from a mirror or a fork. A different ref here splits the entrypoint from the payload and result.json records upstream.ref_consistent false.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_repo_url
keys.help: The repository upstream's installer clones the payload from. Passed as its -r flag.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_checksum
keys.help: The sha256 of upstream's install.sh at the pinned ref. Normally comes from the per-release data file. Upstream's -b does not replace this: -b pins the payload, this pins the entrypoint.

keys.name: tpot_install_type
keys.help: Which T-Pot edition to install. NOT what upstream is told: upstream is always invoked as the sensor type, whose code path never asks for a web credential, and the edition is applied afterwards by copying its compose file over docker-compose.yml. The edition also decides which honeypot takes over TCP/22.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_extra_flags
keys.help: Extra flags appended verbatim to upstream's invocation. These become argv: never put a secret here. Do not put -s, -t, -u, -p, -b or -r here either; this project sets all six and a second copy would undo an invariant.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_env
keys.help: Non-secret environment for upstream's installer, merged over LANG=C.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=C.UTF-8. Never set either to C: ansible-core refuses to start under a non-UTF-8 locale, and ansible-core is what drives the install.

keys.name: tpot_driver_install_timeout
keys.help: Seconds of silence tolerated while upstream's installer downloads and builds.

keys.name: tpot_reboot_policy
keys.help: never exits 20 and arms a post-boot verification unit instead of rebooting. The host reboots anyway: upstream's playbook installs a root cron job that reboots it nightly, at an hour and minute it randomises per install. The closing notice names the time this box got; crontab -l -u root is where it lives.

keys.name: tpot_min_memory_mb
keys.help: Hard floor for memory in MiB, and the one floor that is not compared with itself. MemTotal is physical RAM minus what firmware and the kernel reserved before anything could count it -- 3.7 to 3.9 per cent on three of this project's own guests -- so a machine provisioned with exactly this figure reports less than it. The measurement is therefore compared against 95 per cent of this value, 7782 MiB at the default 8192, and below THAT the run stops. The floor itself is not lowered to achieve it: 8192 is upstream's own stated Sensor minimum, and both numbers are named in every record and every refusal. lib/preflight.sh applies the factor before the play and roles/preflight applies it again once the play is running, both with whole-percent integer arithmetic so the two cannot disagree at one value.

keys.name: tpot_warn_memory_mb
keys.help: Warning threshold for memory in MiB. Not adjusted by the tolerance the floor carries, because it blocks nothing: below it a run warns and continues.

keys.name: tpot_min_cpus
keys.help: Hard floor for CPU count. Below it the run stops. Upstream states no CPU figure at all and its installer contains no CPU check, so the floor sits below both disputed inherited numbers.

keys.name: tpot_warn_cpus
keys.help: Warning threshold for CPU count.

keys.name: tpot_min_disk_gb
keys.help: Hard floor for free disk in GiB, checked on two filesystems. A deliberate deviation BELOW upstream's own stated 128 GB minimum, so that a modest test guest can complete a run.

keys.name: tpot_warn_disk_gb
keys.help: Warning threshold for free disk in GiB.

keys.name: tpot_required_ports
keys.help: Ports that must be free before the install starts; 64294 is sensor-to-hive. Port 22 may be held by the host's own sshd. Upstream additionally refuses tcp/25, tcp/53 and udp/53, which this list cannot express and preflight must cover separately.

keys.name: tpot_admin_ssh_port
keys.help: Where administrative SSH moves to. Read by preflight, verification, the notice and result.json.

keys.name: tpot_dashboard_port
keys.help: Where the dashboard listens, over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate.

keys.name: tpot_elasticsearch_port
keys.help: Where the search engine listens. Verification asserts it is reachable on loopback only.

keys.name: tpot_min_containers
keys.help: How many running containers a healthy T-Pot has. Shipped unset, from the per-release data file, and COUNTED AT PIN TIME FROM compose/<edition>.yml, NEVER GUESSED: neither upstream file states a number.

keys.name: tpot_verify_retries
keys.help: How many times the post-reboot half of verification retries a wait, and it bounds TWO of them: each listener check, and the wait for the running container count to reach its floor. They share one pair of knobs on purpose -- a box slow enough to need more patience for one is slow for the same reason in the other. Raising it buys time and moves no threshold: the container floor and every verdict stay where they are.

keys.name: tpot_verify_delay
keys.help: Seconds between verification retries. With the default 30 retries this gives each wait 300 seconds. A wait also leaves early on a decided answer -- the floor reached, or the T-Pot unit dead so nothing more is coming.

keys.name: tpot_web_env_force
keys.help: Whether to overwrite a dashboard credential already present in T-Pot's .env. Upstream never writes one on this project's path, so it matters only for a re-run or for genuser.sh. Only WEB_USER is ever touched; LS_WEB_USER is upstream-managed.

keys.name: tpot_upstream_telemetry
keys.help: Governs upstream's Sicherheitstacho community submission, and nothing else. There is no .env key and no upstream flag: off removes the ewsposter service block from docker-compose.yml and then asserts it is gone. Quote the value in YAML: bare off is a boolean there.

keys.name: tpot_force_unsupported_os
keys.help: Relax THIS project's matrix check. Recorded in result.json. It cannot touch upstream's own /etc/os-release gate, which runs before upstream reads any flag and has no override; reaching an older release is the legacy tier, meaning an older pinned ref, not this flag.

keys.name: tpot_force_low_resources
keys.help: Continue below the hard resource floors. Recorded in result.json.

keys.name: tpot_force_reinstall
keys.help: Re-run upstream's installer on a box that already has T-Pot. Recorded in result.json.

keys.name: tpot_firewall_mode
keys.help: Reserved. none is the only accepted value in this release: this installer adds no firewall rules of its own. That is not the same as the host's filtering being untouched -- upstream sets the firewalld public zone to ACCEPT and SELinux to permissive on Red Hat family hosts.

keys.name: tpot_install_deps
keys.help: Whether install.sh may install its own prerequisites.

keys.name: tpot_state_dir
keys.help: Where result.json and the post-boot verification marker live. Flag-only: use --state-dir DIR.

keys.name: tpot_log_dir
keys.help: Where the per-run transcript lives. Flag-only: use --log-dir DIR.

keys.name: tpot_runtime_dir
keys.help: The 0700 tmpfs directory for this run, resolved by install.sh. Flag-only: use --runtime-dir DIR.

keys.name: ioc_forwarding_enabled
keys.help: Reserved. Setting it true fails: forwarding is not implemented in this release.

keys.name: ioc_endpoint_url
keys.help: Reserved. Where indicators would be sent: one whole URL, not a base plus an identifier.

keys.name: ioc_sensor_id
keys.help: Reserved. Which sensor sent an indicator. An opaque string, deliberately not a UUID.

keys.name: ioc_auth_header_name
keys.help: Reserved. The name of the authentication header.

keys.name: ioc_auth_header_value
keys.help: Reserved. SECRET. The whole header value, so any scheme is expressible without an enumeration.
